catholic-encyclopedia-1913-charles-nerin:
An entry on Charles Nerinckx, the Belgian missionary priest called the Apostle of Kentucky and founder of the Sisters of Loretto. Born at Herffelingen in 1761, the eldest of fourteen children, he studied at Louvain and Mechlin, was ordained in 1785, and worked among labourers at Mechlin cathedral. Hunted by the French Directoire for his ministry, he hid for four years at Dendermonde hospital before sailing to America in 1804.

Bishop Carroll assigned him to Kentucky in 1805, a district over two hundred miles long covering nearly half the state. Nerinckx lived in the saddle, founding a congregation or building a church in nearly every year of his mission. He refused the bishopric of New Orleans and crossed the Atlantic twice to recruit helpers. In 1812 he founded the Sisters of Loretto at the Foot of the Cross to secure Catholic schooling for children. He died at Ste. Genevieve, Missouri, in 1824.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-peter-hubert-: This biographical entry profiles Peter Hubert Evermode Backx, a Premonstratensian abbot of the 1800s, tracing his career, his abbacy, and his place as the 1913 editors recorded it. A compact life from the encyclopedia's monastic gallery, preserved among its medieval founders.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pierre-jean-b: Pierre-Jean Beckx was the Belgian Jesuit who led the Society as its general for thirty-four years. This entry traces his generalate, his trials, and his sanctity. The general of the exiled Society: his long wise rule steadied the exiled order.
